# Issue #112: last page is followed by a phantom empty page

With 9 items and `per_page=3`, `paginate(items, 3, 3)` says `has_next` is true and
`total_pages` is 4. Page 4 then comes back as an empty list instead of an error.
This only happens when the item count is an exact multiple of `per_page`; 10 items
at 3 per page is fine. Fix `pager/paginate.py`.

The bug is in `page_count`: `total_items // per_page + 1` overcounts by one when the item count is an exact multiple of `per_page` (9 items, 3/page → 4 pages instead of 3). The fix is to use ceiling division, keeping the "at least 1 page" rule for empty collections.

assert r['items'] == [6, 7, 8], r
assert r['total_pages'] == 3, r
assert not r['has_next'], r

    paginate(list(range(9)), 4, 3)
    raise AssertionError('should have raised')
except ValueError as e:
    print('page 4 correctly rejected:', e)
# non-multiple still fine
assert page_count(10, 3) == 4
assert page_count(0, 3) == 1
assert page_count(1, 3) == 1
assert page_count(3, 3) == 1
assert page_count(4, 3) == 2
print('all sanity checks passed')

Fixed and verified. The bug was in `page_count` in `pager/paginate.py`: it used `total_items // per_page + 1`, which always adds an extra page when the item count is an exact multiple of `per_page` (9 items ÷ 3 = 3 pages, but the formula returned 4). That phantom 4th page made `has_next` true on the real last page and returned an empty list instead of raising.

The fix uses proper ceiling division — `(total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page` — with a special case returning 1 for an empty collection, preserving the documented "always at least 1 page" behavior. Verified: `paginate(range(9), 3, 3)` now reports `total_pages=3` with `has_next=False`, page 4 raises `ValueError`, non-multiple counts (10 items → 4 pages) and empty collections are unchanged, and the existing test suite passes.

arguments.summary: Fixed the phantom empty page in pager/paginate.py: page_count() used `total_items // per_page + 1`, which overcounts by one page when the item count is an exact multiple of per_page (e.g. 9 items at 3/page gave 4 pages, so page 3 had has_next=True and page 4 returned an empty list). Replaced it with ceiling division `(total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page`, keeping the documented at-least-1-page rule for empty collections. Verified with the existing test suite plus sanity checks: 9/3 now yields 3 pages with has_next=False on the last page and page 4 raises ValueError; 10/3 still yields 4 pages; empty input still yields 1 page.
